problem: A locally authored AC1027 MTEXT with AcDbEntity group 48=3.5, AcDbMText rotation group 50=30, then a type-75-first main-subclass column run with group 48=12.5 and group 50 count/heights 2,10,20 was accepted with callback linetype scale 12.5 and angle 20. Column width overwrote the common field, column heights overwrote rotation, and the column fields were otherwise not retained.

authority.scope: The table lists MTEXT main-subclass column fields 75,76,78,79,48,49 and 50; 50 also denotes rotation. Group 50's documented height list has a count followed by its values.
authority.leadLimit: This peer issue independently reports the same class of scope collision; it is neither a normative field-order authority nor evidence of native producer compatibility.

implementation.carrier: A separate final DRW_MTextLegacyColumns runtime subtype carries a shared immutable Source with ordered numeric column groups and the observed input revision and encoding. Its source/lease is shared by copies and the standard adapter accounts for retained source bytes and preserves the dynamic type. The base DRW_MText layout, callbacks and ordinary non-column behavior remain unchanged. A consumer that deliberately copies into the base class loses the separate carrier.
implementation.grammar: Only a standalone, explicitly AcDbMText-scoped run with group 75 first is accepted. Groups 76,78,79,48,49 must each appear once in any order after 75 and before any height group; type is 0..2, count 0..4096 and flags 0/1. An optional group-50 height count must be an integral double in 1..4096, immediately followed by exactly that many contiguous group-50 finite values. The separate group-76 count and height count are retained independently. A prospective column field before 75, duplicate/incomplete fields, interrupted or excessive height sequences, extra ambiguous 50 or a mixed Embedded Object refuses the read without a callback. Foreign explicitly marked subclass group 75 and non-column MTEXT retain previous handling. A group 50 observed before the first column type is treated as the ordinary rotation under this bounded profile; more general out-of-order grammars remain unresolved.
implementation.readBudget: The source owner and each retained group are charged to the existing retained-byte budget before vector publication; a shared immutable owner holds the lease until its last copy is destroyed. The adapter's separate retained-entity estimate includes the source owner and vector.
implementation.output: This is an input-only carrier. Direct DXF writing refuses it and shared entity preflight also rejects a forged public type tag through inherited POINT/LINE/TEXT entries. Shared DWG entity preflight latches required failure for this subtype, so a consumer ignoring writeMText or inherited writer false cannot publish a drawing with the entity silently omitted. Both routes preserve the destination on refusal. R2018 embedded-column fields are not used to model the legacy run.

validation.focusedCoverage: Generated ASCII/Binary inputs verify original linetype and rotation, exact ordered captured column values, source version/encoding, XDATA, ordinary base-only callback and non-column compatibility, foreign subclass and non-column misplaced group 48, alternate allowed field ordering, ambiguous/incomplete/out-of-order/duplicate or interrupted inputs, bounded resource refusal and same-reader retry, and immutable-source sharing by copies. The stock adapter retains the subtype. DXF and AC1018 DWG writers fail atomically even when callbacks ignore false and public tags are forged through MTEXT/TEXT/LINE/POINT paths; an explicit base-only downgrade retries successfully. Separate generated AC1032 embedded-column ASCII/Binary read/write/read controls preserve both height fields and the common scale/rotation.
validation.fixtures: All drawings are locally authored temporary files and removed; no DWG/DXF fixtures were committed.

limits: This carrier records typed group values and source revision/encoding, not original lexical bytes or authenticated provenance. Binary group-50 counts are tested as locally generated doubles according to the library classifier; Autodesk's text describes a count as Int16 and native binary framing is unqualified. The bounded order is not a producer-wide schema, and no native rendering, linked-column semantics, conversion, or support claim is promoted. Copying to a base DRW_MText intentionally removes the loss guard. Other source grammars, record ordering, independent producer witnesses and native/platform tests remain open.
